Package org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.impl

Class ProcessContextResolver

java.lang.Object
org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.impl.ProcessContextResolver
public final class ProcessContextResolver extends Object
Resolves the declared contextVariables allowlist of an AI agent service task into a structured block that is appended to the system prompt.

Why an allowlist, and why names rather than expressions

Nothing reaches the model unless the modeler wrote its name into the contextVariables input — isolation by declaration rather than by omission. The input carries variable names, not ${expression} values, because the Connect boundary (ConnectorVariableScope.writeToRequest) unwraps every TypedValue before the connector sees it: the type, and for files the filename and mime type, are gone by then. Reading execution.getVariableTyped(name, false) here keeps all of it.

Why the values are read without deserializing

getVariableTyped(name) would deserialize an ObjectValue, which fails with ClassNotFoundException whenever the payload class is not on the connector's classloader — a routine situation for customer POJOs. The non-deserializing read never fails that way: JSON/XML-serialized objects are rendered from their serialized form, and opaque formats (Java serialization) are rendered as a descriptor instead of as garbage.

Prompt injection

Process variables routinely hold user- or document-sourced text. Values are therefore escaped, and any literal AgentConnectorConstants.CONTEXT_BLOCK_OPEN / AgentConnectorConstants.CONTEXT_BLOCK_CLOSE token inside a value has its leading < replaced by &lt;, so a variable cannot close the block early and have its remainder read as an instruction. The block header additionally tells the model that the content is data, not instructions.
